clue.text: Rule expecting state to renounce leadership

indicators.note: giving up the lead means the front letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: being pregnant is the state of expecting a baby

explanation.surface: A ruling body is urged to make the nation give up its leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to renounce leadership' drops P, the first letter of PREGNANCY, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnancy is the condition of reigning, so it is a formal synonym for rule or sovereignty.

clue.text: One's crisis forced annulment

indicators.note: the letters are forced into a different arrangement

parts.note: contracted form taken letter for letter, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A personal crisis forces a contract to be cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges ONES plus CRISIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescission is the legal cancelling of a contract, an annulment.

clue.text: Having kittens held by gun, one sees stars

indicators.note: being held by means sitting inside the other word

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun
to litter is to give birth to a litter of young
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A panicking person held at gunpoint sees stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having kittens' looks like panic, but here it means giving birth; gat is American gangster slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The glitterati are fashionable celebrities, the stars of the social scene.

clue.text: Soldier binding old foe, time troops practised selfrestraint

indicators.note: binding means wrapping around the other pieces

parts.note: a soldier ant is a type of worker ant
Germany was Britain's enemy in two world wars
an age is a long time
men means troops

explanation.surface: A soldier ties up a former enemy while the rest show restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: A soldier ant is a type of ant; the old foe is Germany, Britain's enemy in two world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger management is therapy in which people learn self-control over their temper.

clue.text: Mini breakfast served up in favourite pub for political opportunist

parts.note: the Mini is a small car
a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: the reversed breakfast sits in the pub, so in places it inside the bar

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means reversed upward

parts.note: an egg is a breakfast item

explanation.surface: A small breakfast is served in a favourite pub for a political chancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses EGG to GGE, put 'in' BAR. Mini is the British small car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpetbagger is an outsider seeking political advantage, an opportunist.

clue.text: Bowler getting out

parts.note: reads like a cricketer dismissing a batsman, but means a hat that is going out of fashion, with the phrase meaning outdated

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler gets batsmen out; here the bowler is the round felt hat, and 'out' means unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a hat and an out-of-date thing is said to be passé, so an outmoded bowler fits both senses.

clue.text: Hit catches a European (English), resulting in shiner

indicators.note: catches means holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: to lam is to thrash
a Serb is a European

explanation.surface: A punch landing on a European gives him a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: A shiner is slang for a black eye, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a light that shines intensely, so it is something that shines.

clue.text: Cue for "Action!", say, essential to leading men

indicators.note: essential to means at the heart of the other word

parts.note: heroes are the leading men
eg means for example, which is what say means

explanation.surface: A director's cue for action is central to the leading men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential to' places EG at the heart of HEROES.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said by someone about to take the plunge, a spoken cue to act.

clue.text: See 23
They would get their kicks after beginning to snog liberal-minded types

indicators.note: the footballers' word comes after the single letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from snog

parts.note: wingers are footballers who kick the ball down the flanks

explanation.surface: Thrill-seekers looking for kicks start kissing open-minded people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes S from snog; 'after' puts WINGERS behind it. The kicks are football kicks, not thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingers are people of free-and-easy, permissive habits, especially sexually liberated ones.

clue.text: He demands much interest where American river runs

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the United States
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A moneylender lives on the bank of an American river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river; R for runs comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant rates, so he is a lender demanding high interest.

clue.text: "Tales of the Unexpected", book which is irritating

indicators.note: something unexpected is out of its expected order

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A book of strange tales proves annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected' rearranges TALESOFTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal infection makes the skin between toes itch, so it is something irritating.

clue.text: With nothing to lose, I,note, judge interrupts clergyman, impatient speaker

indicators.note: to lose a letter means it is removed from the words it sits among

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: breaking into a word means sitting inside it

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A man of the cloth is interrupted by a judge while someone else keeps cutting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With nothing to lose' drops O from I NOTE, leaving INTE; 'interrupts' puts J inside the clergyman. J for judge is a legal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjector is someone who breaks in on others' speech, an impatient speaker who will not wait.

clue.text: Is element in China specious?

parts.note: Ming was a Chinese dynasty
lead is a chemical element

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a part of China is deceptive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain, which fits Ming vases, but here it stands for the dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious arguments seem plausible but deceive, so they are deceptive.

clue.text: See 3
Noncommittal gesture to the 4's noisy booty?

indicators.note: noisy means the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: the 4 is the carpetbagger of 4-down, so his belongings are his
what a carpetbagger bags is a carpet, a rug

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the haul of a political chancer with a careless gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 4-down is CARPETBAGGER: his booty is a carpet. Said quickly, 'his rug' runs together into the answer, the HIS slurred to SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug of the shoulders is the classic gesture of indifference or not committing oneself.

clue.text: Tears of joy? Well I never!

definitions.meaning: a playful reading as happy sorrow

explanation.definitionFit: Good grief is an exclamation of surprise, and read literally it is pleasant sorrow.

clue.text: British, then French, go in with a woman of elegance

parts.note: aller is the French verb to go

explanation.surface: A Briton, then a Frenchman, joins an elegant woman.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLER is French for 'to go'; 'then' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer, famed for grace and poise.

clue.text: Exposed bottom of elf should get beaten

parts.note: something exposed is out in the open

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter, here taken from elf

parts.note: ought means should

explanation.surface: An elf with a bare bottom deserves a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom of' picks F from elf.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outfought is to be beaten in a fight; here it is the past participle, defeated.

clue.text: Spicy singer a sweet one?

parts.note: Mel B was one of the Spice Girls pop group

explanation.surface: A singer with spice wonders whether she is a sweet one.
explanation.walkthrough: Mel B was Scary Spice of the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach Melba is a famous dessert named after the soprano Nellie Melba.

clue.text: Get it and assume imprecise?

indicators.note: the letters are not set down in their exact order, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to grasp a point and take a rough view of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprecise' shuffles GETIT plus ASSUME; the whole clue also describes the answer, an assumption made roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A guesstimate is an estimate based on guesswork, an imprecise assumption.

clue.text: Taking into account every capital, if New Delhi is anyone's, it's mine!

definitions.text: Taking into account every capital, if New Delhi is anyone's, it's mine!

parts.words: Taking into account every capital, if New Delhi is anyone's, it's mine!
parts.note: of all the world's capitals, the country speaking claims New Delhi as its own

explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital of this country, so it alone can claim that city as its capital.

clue.text: See 7
Impressive performance having to open vessel

parts.note: to start is to open
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A great performance is needed to open a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the main act or the outstanding performance in a show.

clue.text: Get stricken boat home

indicators.note: a stricken vessel is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A wrecked boat is brought back to harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stricken' rearranges BOAT to OBTA.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get or acquire it.

clue.text: Frogs, perhaps, stupid people

definitions.meaning: frogs are among the small creatures living in ponds
a slang insult for people regarded as the lowest of the low

explanation.surface: Frogs are dismissed as dimwits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pond life literally means creatures of ponds and figuratively despicable or stupid people.

clue.text: Bit of neck, or bum?

definitions.meaning: the nape, the back of the neck by which an animal is grabbed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to grab a neck or a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, and a scruff is also a scruffy, untidy person.

clue.text: Neat hand

definitions.meaning: in poker, five cards in sequence

explanation.definitionFit: A drink served neat is taken straight, and a straight is a poker hand of consecutive cards.
